links.outcome: Gender subgroup F1 gap in LLM emergency triage versus 0.05 threshold
links.effect: Per-subgroup confusion matrix stratification found gender ΔF1 of 0.020, within the 0.05 governance threshold; bias was class-directional rather than demographically concentrated.
links.quote: Evaluated on the MIMIC-IV Full Emergency dataset (N=300-1,000), FairGuard achieves a gender ΔF1 of 0.020, well within threshold, while identifying RAG corpus composition as the root cause of conservative triage bias (50.9% Urgent → Non-Urgent misclassification), establishing that the observed bias is class-directional rather than demographically concentrated.

links.outcome: Under-triage of urgent patients by LLM triage support
links.effect: 50.9% of Urgent cases were misclassified as Non-Urgent, a conservative triage bias attributed to RAG corpus composition.

screen.reason: The study designs and empirically tests a continuous fairness governance framework (guardrail architecture with bias auditing, consent gating, and blockchain-anchored threshold enforcement) for an LLM emergency triage system using MIMIC-IV data.

primary.practice: continuous fairness auditing and threshold enforcement guardrail
